newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN executive quits over insider trading.
newsitem.headline: ABN executive quits over insider trading.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV said on Wednesday its board member Louis de Bievre had resigned due to his indirect involvement in an insider trading case.

"This case refers to a situation whereby Mr De Bievre's wife in 1992 traded in shares of a listed company at a time when she was aware of certain specific information related to this company based upon remarks made by her husband," ABN AMRO said.
It added that De Bievre had informed the chairman of ABN AMRO's management board about the existence of this case yesterday.

In subsequent contacts between the public prosecutor and ABN AMRO's management board, the public prosecutor had stated that De Bievre's wife and not De Bievre himself had been guilty of insider trading, ABN AMRO said.
ABN AMRO said the case would not go to trial as the matter had been settled in an out of court arrangement with the Dutch public prosecutor in accordance with Dutch criminal law.

ABN AMRO said its management board respected De Bievre's decision and regretted that his long and successful career at the bank had ended in this way. De Bievre's resignation was with immediate effect, it added.
